# Ongoing EU Clinical Trials

ESVONC attaches great importance to innovation and evidence-based medicine in the field of veterinary oncology. Therefore, we are happy to share with you with a monthly overview of ongoing canine and feline oncology trials in Europe. We are convinced that knowledge of these trials will enhance collaboration between researchers and clinicians, thus increasing recruitment for clinical trials and treatment options for dogs and cats.
Please find below a non-exhaustive listing of ongoing trials as gathered in the Oncowaf database. For more details about these trials, please visit https://oncowaf.be/en/ClinicalTrials.

If you have an ongoing clinical trial and would like to add it to the Oncowaf clinical trial database and this mailing, please contact contact@oncowaf.com. This list is an intiative of dr. Laetitia Cicchelero (DVM, PhD, Cross-health coordinator @ Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Ghent University). Laetitia is initiator and inspirer of ONCOWAF. ESVONC wishes to thank Laetitia for her efforts to create this useful overview.

Clinical trials

How can I find an ongoing clinical trial?

Via the search button, you can perform a targeted search for canine clinical trials. In order to do this, tick -if known- the box of your dog’s tumour type (‘Select tumour type’) and/or the countries (‘Select location’) for which you wish to know whether clinical trials are ongoing.

Afterwards, a list of trials for which your dog might be eligible will appear. The listed information is limited to

  * Treatment centre where the trial is available
  * In/exclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria describe the criteria necessary for your dog to participate in the trial (e.g. inoperable tumour). Exclusion criteria describe conditions that exclude possible participation to the trial (e.g. concomitant chemotherapy).
  * Contact information: phone number and e-mail address of the trial’s contact person, webpage with more information on the trial.

For more details on the trial, we recommend you to contact the researchers via the listed contact info.

Our database is currently limited to European trials. If you are interested in clinical trials from the USA, you can find these through this link

# Klinische Studien

Image: UTZ_KT_Radiologie_Onkologie_Vorbereitung_Hund

In unserem wissenschaftlichen Engagement ist die klinische Forschung ein wichtiger Bestandteil, und oft können wir unseren Patienten neue Behandlungsoptionen anbieten und gleichzeitig wertvolle Informationen im Kampf gegen Krebs gewinnen. Dies geschieht allerdings nur mit ausdrücklicher Erlaubnis des Tierbesitzers.

## Aktuelle klinische Studien

  * Strahlensensivität von Hirntumoren (Meningiomen) bei Hunden
  * Lattice- oder SBRT Strahlentherapie bei grossen Tumoren
  * Plattenepithelkarzinom der Maulhöhle bei Katzen: «Nebenwirkungen und Tumorkontrolle der ultraschnellen (FLASH) Protonenbestrahlung im Vergleich zur konventionellen Protonentherapie».
  * Hirntumoren: «Chemoradiation bei hochgradigen Gliomen».

Ist Ihr Hund oder Ihre Katze betroffen? Dann könnte Ihr Tier an einer dieser Studien teilnehmen. Informieren Sie sich jetzt!

# Radiation therapy clinical trials for dogs and cats

These studies test radiation protocols, radiation combined with another treatment and newer approaches such as FLASH or lattice radiotherapy.

24 current studies and treatment programs in this category

This is not a directory of every hospital that offers standard radiation therapy. It contains current treatment studies in the Vet Cancer Care Finder catalog.

## Current listings

One study may appear under more than one treatment type when it combines approaches. Review the full eligibility criteria and confirm current enrollment with the study team.

### Lattice or SBRT radiotherapy for large inoperable canine tumors

University of Zurich — Division of Radiation Oncology · Switzerland

Ongoing European oncology clinical trial — listed by Oncowaf

What is being offered: Randomized therapeutic comparison of Lattice radiotherapy and SBRT for large inoperable canine tumors, or when radiotherapy is preferred to surgery. Five consecutive daily treatment sessions. Research biopsies are requested when safely accessible; the treating team confirms final eligibility and consent. Single enrolling center: University of Zurich Veterinary Hospital.

Who may qualify: Confirmed cancer diagnosis required; Active tumor required; Large inoperable or rt preferred

Costs / coverage: 🟠 Partially funded. Owners pay the initial consultation, radiation-planning CT and anesthesia for the radiation treatments. Research funding covers the radiation itself and CT or MRI follow-up examinations at six and twelve months.

Contact: University of Zurich Radiation Oncology — +41 44 635 81 12

Location

  * Universitäres Tierspital Zürich, Winterthurerstrasse 204, 8057 Zürich, Switzerland

Official study / enrollment information →

### Palliative radiation + frunevetmab for feline bone-invasive oral SCC

University of Pennsylvania · USA

Active - Recruiting

What is being offered: Pilot palliative study for feline bone-invasive oral SCC.

Who may qualify: Confirmed cancer diagnosis required; Active tumor required; No metastasis; Mandibular or maxillary bone lysis; chemotherapy washout: 21 days; radiation washout: 21 days; Immunotherapy and anti ngf washout 21d

### Chemoradiation for canine high-grade glioma

University of Zurich Veterinary Hospital · Switzerland

Participation currently possible on the University of Zurich study page

What is being offered: All enrolled dogs receive radiotherapy. Dogs are randomized to temozolomide plus lomustine or placebo to evaluate added chemotherapy for high-grade glioma.

Who may qualify: Active tumor required; Planned radiation; Brain tumor biopsy

Costs / coverage: The university states that biopsy, chemotherapy and study laboratory tests are covered and radiotherapy is discounted; confirm all costs directly.

Contact: Zurich glioma study — +41 44 635 9595; neurologie@vetclinics.uzh.ch

Location

  * Universitäres Tierspital Zürich, Winterthurerstrasse 204, 8057 Zürich, Switzerland

Official study / enrollment information →

### FLASH proton radiotherapy for feline oral squamous cell carcinoma

University of Zurich Veterinary Hospital · Switzerland

Participation currently possible on the University of Zurich study page
Confirm the current estimate and any unrelated care with the Zurich study team.

Contact: University of Zurich study team — Dr. Maximilian Körner; +41 44 635 95 55; onkologie@vetclinics.uzh.ch

Location

  * Universitäres Tierspital Zürich, Winterthurerstrasse 204, 8057 Zürich, Switzerland

Official study / enrollment information →

### FLASH radiotherapy for canine superficial malignant tumors

University Hospital for Companion Animals, University of Copenhagen / Lund University · Denmark

Recruiting/current project — University of Copenhagen lists patients for the 2020–2027 FLASH radiotherapy project

What is being offered: Dogs with a cancer mass in skin, subcutis or oral cavity, including incompletely removed/residual tumor, may participate when there is expected therapeutic benefit. Dogs receive 1–4 radiotherapy treatments over up to four weeks; most receive FLASH and a smaller group conventional radiotherapy. Treatment requires travel within the Copenhagen/Lund collaboration.

Who may qualify: Active tumor required; Superficial or oral tumor; Anesthesia fit; Planned radiation

Costs / coverage: The project states that treatment and follow-up visits are paid by the project; owner is responsible for EU pet passport/rabies requirements for travel to Sweden.

Contact: Betina Børresen — bb@sund.ku.dk

Location

  * Denmark

Official study / enrollment information →

### Radiotherapy plus Lavurchin (SQAP) radiosensitizer for feline oral squamous cell carcinoma

Animal Medical Center, Gifu University · Japan

# Clinical Study for Cats with Mammary Cancer - Information for referring veterinarians

## Why refer your patients?

  * The therapy (GCN2-IN-6) has been carefully tested in preclinical studies and is well-tolerated.
  * Your referred patients will receive standard surgical care plus the investigational therapy.
  * Participation contributes valuable data for advancing cancer treatments in both cats and humans.

## Study design highlights

  * Neo-adjuvant and adjuvant therapy administered around the time of mastectomy.

  * Safety and efficacy are continuously monitored.

  * Feline mammary adenocarcinoma is a validated model for TNBC research.

## Referral process

  * Eligible cats: cats diagnosed with mammary tumors, eligible for surgery.

  * As referring veterinarians, you can retain primary responsibility for routine care; the study team coordinates treatment administration and follow-up.

  * Participation is voluntary, and owners can withdraw at any time.

## Impact:

By referring cats to this study, you are helping advance cutting-edge cancer research, improve therapeutic options, and potentially enhance outcomes for both feline and human patients.

## Contact

Further information can be obtained by mailing Ada Krupa (adriana.krupa@ugent.be) or Hilde de Rooster (hilde.derooster@ugent.be) or by phone (+32 9 264 77 00).

##### Onkologija

V zadnjem času se onkološka obolenja pojavljajo vse pogosteje, kar je posledica daljše življenjske dobe hišnih ljubljencev ter vedno bolj izpopolnjenih diagnostičnih in terapevtskih metod v veterinarski medicini. Onkološki pacienti terjajo poglobljen, predvsem pa celovit pristop. Na Kliniki za kirurgijo in male živali Veterinarske fakultete v Ljubljani se poglobljeno ukvarjamo z onkologijo predvsem psov in mačk. Kot prvi v Sloveniji smo v zdravljenje vpeljali elektrokemoterapijo, kasneje pa še elektrogensko terapijo. Obe zdravljenji se izvajata v splošni anesteziji, ta je potrebna tudi za endoskopske preglede ter odvzem bioptov za patohistološko preiskavo. Klinična dejavnost vključuje diagnostične in terapevtske postopke.
